title: DealMachine Pricing Plans 2026: What Real Estate Investors Need to Know

sections.content: If you are a real estate wholesaler, flipper, or investor shopping for deal-finding software, you have probably come across DealMachine. It is one of the most recognized apps in the space, and for good reason. But before you hand over your credit card, it pays to understand exactly what the DealMachine pricing plans for 2026 look like, what features you actually get at each tier, and whether the cost makes sense for your business model.
DealMachine Pricing Plans for 2026: A Full Breakdown

DealMachine has evolved its pricing structure over the years, moving from a simple per-user model to a more feature-based tiered system. As of 2026, the platform offers three main subscription levels: Starter, Pro, and Team. Each tier stacks on features rather than just adding seats, which changes how investors should evaluate the cost.
Starter Plan

The Starter plan sits at roughly $49 per month when billed annually, or around $59 month-to-month. It gives solo investors access to the core driving-for-dollars feature, basic property data, and a limited number of mail pieces per month — typically around 50. This plan suits someone just testing the waters in wholesaling, particularly in smaller or mid-size markets. However, the low mail credit ceiling means you will hit a wall quickly if you plan to market at any real volume.
Pro Plan

The Pro plan, priced near $99 to $149 per month depending on billing cycle and any promotional pricing, is where most active wholesalers land. You get expanded skip tracing credits, more mail pieces (often 150 to 300 per month), list building tools, and integrations with CRMs like Podio and Follow Up Boss. If you are working active markets like [Atlanta](https://aiwholesail.com/markets/atlanta-ga) or [Dallas](https://aiwholesail.com/markets/dallas-tx), this tier gives you enough horsepower to run consistent campaigns without constantly hitting data walls.
Team Plan

The Team plan starts around $299 per month and scales up based on the number of users and credit volume. It unlocks features like route tracking for multiple drivers, team dashboards, bulk skip tracing, and priority support. Real estate companies with dedicated acquisition teams or multiple wholesale deals closing each month will find this tier the most cost-effective on a per-deal basis.

Always check DealMachine's website for current promotional pricing. The platform regularly runs 20-30% discounts for annual commitments, and new user trials sometimes include bonus mail credits worth $50 or more. Locking in an annual plan during a promo window can save you several hundred dollars over the year.
What Do You Actually Get for the Money?

Beyond the headline price, it is worth examining what DealMachine's core features deliver in practice. The driving-for-dollars tool lets you map routes and tag distressed properties in real time. Property owner data pulls from public records and is often refreshed more frequently than older legacy platforms. Skip tracing allows you to find phone numbers and emails for property owners, which is critical for making direct contact before a property hits the MLS.

items: Driving-for-dollars route tracking and property tagging via mobile app
Owner information lookup including mailing address, phone, and email
Direct mail campaigns sent from within the platform
Skip tracing credits included at Pro and Team tiers
List stacking to layer multiple distress filters (tax delinquency, vacancy, pre-foreclosure)
CRM integrations to push leads into your existing workflow
Comparable sales data to help estimate property value

sections.content: One thing to watch: DealMachine charges separately for skip tracing beyond the monthly allotment. Costs typically run $0.15 to $0.25 per record depending on your plan level. If you are pulling large lists — say 500 to 1,000 leads per month — those overage fees can add $75 to $200 or more to your bill. Factor that into your true monthly cost before comparing plans.
How DealMachine Pricing Compares to Alternatives

The real estate tech space is crowded in 2026. Platforms like PropStream, Batch Leads, and newer AI-driven tools all compete for the same investor dollar. PropStream, for example, offers nationwide MLS data and list building at around $99 per month with no per-record skip tracing fee up to a certain threshold. Batch Leads bundles texting and skip tracing together in a way some investors find more streamlined than DealMachine's module approach.
The best deal-finding tool is not the one with the most features — it is the one your team will actually use consistently every week. A $49 plan you use daily beats a $299 plan collecting dust.

What sets some newer platforms apart is the use of AI to surface motivated seller signals automatically, rather than relying solely on driving neighborhoods or manually stacking lists. If you are investing in competitive markets like [Phoenix](https://aiwholesail.com/markets/phoenix-az), speed to a qualified lead matters more than ever. AI-assisted tools can flag properties showing multiple distress indicators before they appear on anyone's radar.
Is DealMachine Worth It in 2026? Key Questions to Ask

No software subscription is worth it in a vacuum. The right question is whether the platform generates enough deal flow to justify the monthly cost. A single wholesale assignment fee of $10,000 to $20,000 easily covers a year of any DealMachine subscription. The real metric is conversion: how many leads does the tool generate each month, and how many of those convert to contracts?

items: How many deals do you close per month, and what is your average assignment fee or profit?
Are you a solo investor or managing a team that needs multi-user access?
Do you rely on driving for dollars, or do you prefer list-based outreach?
How important is direct mail versus texting or cold calling in your marketing mix?
Do you need MLS comparable data, or do you pull comps from a separate source?

sections.content: If driving for dollars is your primary lead generation method, DealMachine is hard to beat at the Starter or Pro level. If you rely more on list pulling and skip tracing at volume, you may find that competitors offer better value per record. Savvy investors often run two platforms simultaneously during a 30-day trial period to compare lead quality before committing.

Before projecting ROI on any new software, run your potential deals through a free Deal Calculator like the one at [aiwholesail.com/tools/wholesale-deal-calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/wholesale-deal-calculator). Plug in your estimated ARV, repair costs, and desired profit margin to see exactly how many deals you need to close each month to justify the subscription cost.
Getting the Most Out of Any Plan You Choose

Whichever DealMachine tier you select, the investors who get the best ROI share a few habits. They set a consistent driving schedule — at minimum two to three sessions per week — and they follow up with every tagged property at least three times before moving on. Direct mail response rates typically average 1% to 3%, which means you need volume and persistence to generate steady deal flow. The platform is a tool; your follow-up system is what closes deals.

It also helps to layer DealMachine data with other signals. Cross-referencing a driving-for-dollars list with tax delinquency records or probate filings, for example, can dramatically improve the quality of your outreach. List stacking is available at higher tiers but can also be done manually with county data if you are on a tighter budget.
